sources.note: Introduces GSM8K, 8.5K grade-school math word problems, and shows that training a verifier to rank many sampled solutions beats finetuning the generator directly.
sources.title: Training Verifiers to Solve Math Word Problems

sources.note: Measures not how far six frontier models move under steering pressure but what kind of response they give when they decline, finds several response modes belonging to a single model, and then traces the largest within-model split to a linearly decodable and causally steerable direction in an open-weight model's residual stream.
sources.title: Divergent Response Modes in Frontier Language Models Under Steering Pressure

sources.note: Uses chain-of-thought about required capabilities as training-time supervision for a skill retriever -- distilled from a teacher in stage one and refined by retrieval-rewarded GRPO in stage two -- so that at inference the model encodes the bare query with no generation at all.
sources.title: SkillReason: Reasoning-Enhanced Agent Skill Retrieval for Implicit User Requests

sources.note: Builds an industrial-safety reasoning benchmark from two pipelines -- program execution over safety scene graphs, and evidence graphs extracted from real accident-investigation reports -- and shows that general multimodal capability does not transfer to it while a 9B model fine-tuned on its chain-of-thought split matches frontier systems.
sources.title: SafeSceneReason: A Multimodal Reasoning Benchmark Connecting Industrial Hazards with Accident Knowledge

sources.note: Turns the hidden-role game Avalon into a diagnostic instrument rather than an arena, decomposing theory of mind into a 2x2 taxonomy of perspective-constrained binary statements, and shows by probing, ground-truth injection and steering that models represent the right answer internally while failing to say it.
sources.title: Avalon-ToM-Bench: Evaluating Fine-Grained Theory of Mind via Asymmetric Game Mechanics

sources.note: Generates financial reasoning benchmarks from executable computation trees over real tables so that answers are correct by construction with no model in the labelling loop, exposes four independently controllable difficulty axes, and finds that unit and scale perturbations collapse the strongest model from 98.4 percent to 3.0.
sources.title: V-FiLLM: Verified Financial LLM Reasoning Benchmark

instructions:
Write the wiki definition for 'benchmark design'.

The sources below are every archived paper and talk that mentions it. Define it as they use it: if they disagree, say so; if the term is used loosely, say that too.

`related` is the one part of the note nothing can work out on its own. The wiki already links entities that turn up in the same summary; what it cannot see is the neighbour a reader would actually want next — the generation before this one, the benchmark it was built to beat, the method it replaces. Name those. Leave the list empty rather than repeating what the sources already put side by side.

Rules:
- Write in en.
- Ground every statement in the supplied material. If something is not stated,
  leave the field empty rather than inferring it.
- No marketing language. Prefer the specific number over the adjective.
- Return one JSON object matching the schema exactly. No prose around it.

aliases: string - other names the sources use for the same thing
output_schema.definition: string - two to four sentences defining the entity as the cited sources use it, not as a textbook would
output_schema.kind: string - one of: concept, method, dataset, model
related: string - name of a neighbouring entity worth linking to. Kept as you give it and never derived away, so name what a reader should turn to next rather than what happens to appear alongside this. Answering again replaces the whole list; an empty list retracts

result.definition: How an evaluation is constructed, and across 6 sources a subject the archive treats as consequential rather than clerical. Three design decisions recur with measured consequences. Generating answers by construction rather than by labelling removes a model from the loop entirely -- one benchmark builds items from executable computation trees over real tables so answers are correct by construction, and exposes four independently controllable difficulty axes, which is what lets it show unit and scale perturbations collapsing a frontier model from 98.4 to 3.0 percent. Deciding what counts as the same problem is a judgement that then defines the result: a symbolic variabilisation is hand-built by experts, so the feasible domains encode a view about identity, and a loose metric granting partial credit narrows the reported drops by an order of magnitude while separating memorisation from inconsistency. And model-mediated construction is pervasive and worth stating -- one benchmark's candidates are filtered, reviewed and audited by models throughout, so what it calls a natural request means what those models judged to be one, with human involvement confined to adjudicating disagreements. The archive's oldest source in this set is the one that introduced a benchmark and its verifier together, which remains the pattern the corpus rewards.
